Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, here's a synthesized clear and concise answer to your question:

A chemical shift MRI can contribute to the morphologic evaluation of solid breast masses. This imaging technique measures the differences in electrical resonance between different tissues, which can help distinguish between various types of breast lesions.

Chemical shift subtraction, a type of MRI technique that involves subtracting images taken at different frequencies, can be particularly useful in evaluating soft tissue densities and margins of benign lesions in fatty breasts. It can also aid in the morphologic analysis of masses in dense breast tissue.

In addition to chemical shift subtraction, 3D ultrasound validation of the postfire needle position is an efficient adjunct to ultrasound-guided Large-Core Needle Biopsy (LCNB). This technique helps ensure accurate and reliable histological assessments of breast lesions.

Moreover, a comparison between prefilled textured saline breast implants and standard textured saline breast implants has shown significant differences in deflation rates at various time points. Poly Implant Prosthesis prefilled textured saline breast implants have a higher cumulative deflation rate compared to Mentor Siltex implants after 4 years. This suggests that there may be factors contributing to the higher deflation rate, such as possible in vitro deflation before implantation and silicone shell curing technique.

Lastly, partial expander deflation prior to radiotherapy can exacerbate adverse effects, particularly for those located at the lower pole of the expander.

In summary, chemical shift MRI is a valuable tool for morphologic evaluation of solid breast masses, with contributions from chemical shift subtraction and 3D ultrasound validation. Understanding these techniques can help clinicians better diagnose and treat breast lesions, ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes.
